chapter: Chicago in the 1920s: Bix, Armstrong, Morton
title: Recording with Jelly Roll Morton
summary: Howard recalls making a couple of Morton sides after the Orient trip and a collector asking him to identify players on records.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: When did you make those records with Morton?
26, 25, something like that. I think it was after I came back off of the TKK trip.
From the Orient? How many sides did you make? Do you remember? No. Did you just make one record date with it?
No. No I made a couple, but I don't even remember the numbers. Well one was Sun Bay Suits, huh? Yeah, that's right.
Do you play this violin solo on Sun Bay Suits, huh?
Well I think there are two violins on that record. Have you heard the record recently? No. Or when you come to New York, I play it.

You know John Stein in Chicago? Yes. He comes up to my house and he wants me to recognize, you know, see if I could tell who was playing. He's got this book here, but this record is, I said well that sounds like Mitch, Humpback Mitch, and that sounds like so and so. And then got on another record. He said well who's playing the clanner on there? I said I don't recognize others. He said well right here it says it's you. You know. Yeah.
